title.en: Three Days to See: the essay in brief

text.en:
Ravi closed his eyes and tried to walk across the room.
"We use our eyes without really seeing," he said.

This essay is by Helen Keller, who was blind and deaf. She imagines what she would do if she could see for just three days. She would want to look at the faces of the people she loves and at the beauty of nature and the world around her.
She says that people with sight often fail to notice the wonders in front of them. She asks every person to use their senses fully, as if they might lose them tomorrow.
The message is to value our senses and notice the world around us. This summary is based on the well-known story or poem and on public chapter notes. Please read the exact text in the textbook, because the textbook version may differ in details.

problem.en: What is the main message of the essay?

text.en: Helen Keller imagines three days of sight.
She notices that people with sight take it for granted.
She asks us to value and use our senses.

prompt.en: A friend says Helen Keller says seeing people already notice everything. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: She says many seeing people miss the wonders around them.
So we should look and listen with care.

points.en: Helen Keller imagines three days of sight.
People often take their senses for granted.
